title: Taser victim had checkered past; Jeffrey Mark Marreel Was Previously Arrested For Assaulting a Peace Officer
article: The Delhi man who died after being Tasered by Norfolk OPP Monday in Fisher's Glen previously faced charges for assaulting a police officer.
Thirty-six-year-old Jeffrey Mark Marreel was charged with assaulting a peace officer and breach of recognizance in June 2005.
At the time, Norfolk OPP said a man at a Delhi address punched an officer in the face when the officer tried to convince him to seek medical treatment.
Later that year, Marreel was involved in an altercation with a former girlfriend.
He was already on probation for an assault charge.
Marreel was also charged with break and enter and breach of probation for an incident that occurred December 2005.
He was seen kicking in a door of a Delhi apartment.
He served 133 days in pre-trial custody and 12 months probation for the break and enter.
In 2006, Marreel was charged with possession of oxycontin and cocaine during Norfolk OPP's Operation Big Mac.
He was sentenced to 45 days time served.
The Special Investigations Unit continues to investigate Monday morning's incident in which police reported Marreel as "combative" and causing a disturbance in Fisher's Glen.

Krista Van Paemel, a Fisher's Glen resident, told CHCH News that another resident had driven past Marreel, who was described as strung out and threatening cars with stairs, and used her phone to call police.
"He described it as holding a three-foot metal plate, like a piece of a staircase over his head and acting like he was going to throw it at the cars or lunging at the cars with it," she said.
SIU spokesperson John Yoannou confirmed investigators had recovered a piece of aluminum stairs and would determine how that was involved in the incident.
An OPP press release said Marreel was Tasered by police at the intersection of Front Road and Fisher's Glen Road.
He was taken into police custody, collapsed at the Norfolk OPP detachment and died at Norfolk General Hospital.
SIU continues to canvas and interview eyewitnesses, residents, family and officers.
Marreel's autopsy was inconclusive Tuesday and more toxicology tests were ordered, Yoannou said.
Investigators will compile a report based on their interviews and forensic evidence.
The report will be submitted to the director of SIU, who will determine if the Norfolk OPP officer's actions were appropriate or if criminal charges will be laid.
